events.content: Move this publishing app to Cache Components in one branch. Keep the newsroom feed on its hourly refresh policy and keep editor preview request-specific. Finish with a production build without leaving routes opted out.
I'll inspect the app structure, git state, and the bundled Next.js docs on Cache Components first.

2  	title: Migrating to Cache Components
3  	nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
4  	description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
5  	related:
6  	  title: Next Steps
7  	  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
10 	    - app/getting-started/caching
11 	    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
12 	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components

15 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
16 	---
17 	
18 	When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).
19 	
20 	The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.
21 	
22 	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
23 	
24 	The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes:
25 	
26 	- **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below.
27 	- **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch.
28 	
29 	Install the skill:
30 	
31 	```bash filename="Terminal"
32 	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
33 	```
34 	
35 	Then give the agent this prompt:
36 	
37 	```prompt
38 	Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill.
39 	```
40 	
41 	## Or migrate by hand
42 	
43 	Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order:
44 	
45 	1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`.
46 	2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time.
47 	3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API.
48 	
49 	Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working. Migrating `unstable_cache` is optional and can happen later.
50 	
51 	Some surfaces have their own steps:
52 	
53 	- For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance.
54 	- For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance.
55 	
56 	The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components.
57 	
58 	## Enable Cache Components
59 	
60 	Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing.
61 	
62 	Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`:
63 	
64

<path>node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/cacheComponents.md</path>
<content>
1 	---
2 	title: cacheComponents
3 	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4 	related:
5 	  links:
6 	    - app/getting-started/caching
7 	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/gu

The app now uses Cache Components on a new branch, `adopt-cache-components`. The production build passes and no route is opted out.

**Changes:**
- **`next.config.ts`**: I replaced the old `experimental.dynamicIO` setting (and its `@ts-expect-error`) with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: I removed `export const revalidate = 3600`. `getStories()` now caches its result with `'use cache'` and `cacheLife('hours')`. That profile refreshes every hour and expires after a day, so the newsroom feed keeps its hourly refresh.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: I removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. The part that reads the `draft-title` cookie is now its own component inside a `<Suspense>` boundary. That part still runs on every request; only the page heading is built ahead of time.

**Verification:**
- `npm run build` finished with exit code 0 and reported "Cache Components enabled":
  ```
  ┌ ○ /
  ├ ○ /_not-found
  ├ ○ /news                1h      1d
  └ ◐ /preview             (Partial Prerender)
  ```
- A search of `app/` and `next.config.ts` found no `instant` opt-outs, no leftover `dynamic`, `revalidate` or `fetchCache` exports, and no `dynamicIO` or `experimental` settings. The only match is an explanatory comment in the news page.

**Other things to know:**
- I haven't committed anything. The branch also carries your earlier uncommitted `package.json` edit, which I didn't touch.
- The build made two changes of its own: it added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `tsconfig.json`'s `include` and created `next-env.d.ts`.
- `.next/` isn't in `.gitignore`, so it now appears as an untracked folder.
- I didn't test the pages in a running server, only the build.
